name: Time Series Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in time series work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in time series work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When multiple time series strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
2. Prefer explicit, readable time series solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
3. Keep time series changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
4. Measure before optimizing any time series bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
5. When time series decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
6. Keep time series outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
7. Re-check edge cases relevant to time series (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic time series advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not silently drop time series edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid introducing new time series abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated time series concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not skip documenting time series assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these time series guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
